correctness.rationale: Necessity follows because two omitted vertices in one blade have identical open signatures. For m>=3, at most one omission per blade leaves enough selected blade-neighbors to ensure open domination and gives pairwise separation within a blade, across blades, and from the center. For m=2, open domination forces every blade full when the center is omitted, while with the center selected at most one blade may be deficient because each lone selected vertex would have signature {c}. These conditions are also sufficient. The resulting independent blade choices give the stated polynomials and minimum counts. The packaged exhaustive checker verifies the definition, characterization, coefficients, and minima on ten parameter pairs through order 13.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification for a standard identification invariant on the canonical one-articulation clique family. It gives every feasible code, not only a minimum, and exposes a sharp structural boundary between friendship blades m=2 and clique blades m>=3. The factorized polynomial simultaneously yields all cardinality counts and exact basis multiplicities, information not supplied by general block-graph bounds or minimum-number algorithms.
